A temperature sensor sits in an insulated box for 24 hours, measuring a
quantity that barely moves. That is deliberate: with the measurand held as
still as the rig allows, what the record actually shows is the *instrument*
— its noise, its slow drift, and how the answer's precision changes with how
long you are willing to average for.

It is the experiment that finally answers a question every earlier session
on this site has left open: averaging always helps, up to a point — where is
that point, and what happens if you keep going past it anyway?

## What you measure {#sec-t3-index-measure}

| Quantity | How | Where it is used later |
|---|---|---|
| Drift | Least-squares fit of a linear term plus a 24 h sinusoid | The bound on any correction assumed constant over a long average |
| Diurnal amplitude | The same fit | Separated from drift; shown to be the room, not the instrument |
| Allan deviation $\sigma_y(\tau)$ | Overlapping estimator on the detrended residual | Identifies the noise process at each averaging time |
| Optimum averaging time $\tau_\mathrm{opt}$ | The minimum of $\sigma_y(\tau)$ | The correct Type A term for the budget — not $s/\sqrt n$ |

: What T3 produces {#tbl-t3-index-outputs}

## Bench {#sec-t3-index-bench}

**Tier 3.** Any supported board, an insulated box built from whatever is at
hand, and — the one hard requirement — a Linux host that can be left running
and connected for over 24 hours. No signal generator, no oscilloscope; the
whole experiment is one long, slow, unattended recording followed by a
compact analysis session.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Equipment left running unattended overnight

This experiment leaves a board and a host running, unattended, for over a
day. Read [the procedure's safety callout](handbook.qmd#sec-t3-procedure)
before starting the log — it covers disabling host sleep, avoiding active
heating elements that are not rated for unattended operation, and labelling
equipment left on a shared bench.
:::

## The reference data is synthetic

It is produced by a seeded generator (`tools/synth/t3_long_term.py`) whose
parameters are plausible placeholders, not measurements — marked
`TODO (Paolo)` in `tools/synth/params/t3.yaml`. It exists so the analysis
templates render, and are checked in continuous integration, without 24
hours of hardware time. Every page that uses it says so.
:::

::: {.content-visible when-profile="instructor"}
## Instructor summary {.instructor-note}

Tier 3, postgraduate, and the only experiment on this site with a 24-hour
unattended phase in the middle. Split it across two short bench sessions a
day apart. Full notes, expected values, common failures and the rubric are in
the [handbook](handbook.qmd#sec-t3-instructor).
:::
